The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00206

In Eastern Investigations and his commentary on The Sources of Wisdom, Fakhr al-Din al-Razi raises a doubt about the claim that a thing comes from potentiality to actuality gradually, although the philosophers agree on it. When something changes, he says, either something comes to be in it or something leaves it. If neither happens—if nothing absent appears and nothing present disappears—then its state at that instant is the same as before, so it has not changed. But change was assumed. Therefore, when a thing changes, something must come to be in it or leave it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00207

Suppose something comes to be in it. That thing was absent and then became present, so it must have a beginning. The beginning cannot be divided, or one part would come before the other and would not be the beginning itself. At its beginning, then, the new thing either exists or does not. If it does not exist, it is still absent and has not begun to exist. If it does exist, then either some part of it remains potential or none does. If none remains, the whole thing came to be at once, not gradually. If some part remains potential, that remaining part is either the very same thing that has come to be—which is impossible, since one thing cannot be present and absent at once—or it is something else. In the latter case, what came first came to be all at once, while what has not yet come to be is wholly absent. No one thing has come to be gradually; there are only separate things following one another. The conclusion, al-Razi says, is that a simple, indivisible thing can only come to be all at once. A thing with many parts can be said to come to be gradually only because each part appears after another. Strictly speaking, anything that has come to be has come to be all at once, and whatever has not come to be is wholly absent. That is his argument.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00208

I reply that Bahmanyar records this objection from earlier philosophers and rejects it. It only denies motion as a continuous whole, he says, which does not exist in external things. What exists is motion as “being between” its endpoints: a flowing state, neither something that has yet to begin nor something that has already come to an end. Most later philosophers took this approach, claiming it was the right philosophical view. But our master and teacher—may his standing remain high—explained that even those who deny motion as a continuous whole still imagine this “being between” as a new, gradually unfolding, continuous thing, whose parts arise one after another. If one thing cannot come to be gradually, how can we imagine it doing so, whether in the external world or in the mind? This misleading argument would prove just as much about imagined things as about external ones, even though everyone agrees it fails. How, then, can it be sound here?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00209

We have proved that a body is continuous and cannot be divided into parts that have no size, as we will explain in our discussion of substance. We also see and feel a body moving from one place to another. That passage is gradual and follows a continuous distance. It is plainly true that a continuous, changing quantity extends along another continuous quantity that remains in place, even if only in the imagination. We should therefore uncover the mistake at the root of the objection. This is not difficult once it is understood: a thing’s being fully present at an instant is different from its existing in time. A thing can exist throughout a stretch of time without its whole self—or any part of it—being present at one instant. Only its endpoint is present then. An endpoint lies outside the thing, because it marks where the thing ends and is absent. The unity of a thing does not rule this out. Motion, time, and similar things have a weak kind of existence: the existence of each part goes with the nonexistence of another. Coming to be gradually does not prevent one continuous thing from existing throughout the whole span of time, which is itself one continuous whole. It only prevents the thing from existing in its entirety, or even in part, at one instant.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00210

Nor must every event have a first instant at which it, or one of its parts, exists. This mistake comes from using the word “beginning” in two different senses. It can mean the endpoint of a thing; or it can mean an instant at which something that comes to be all at once first exists and then remains. Motion does not come to be all at once and then continue. It has no first instant of coming to be, nor does any part of it have one, since each part of motion is motion. It has an endpoint, and that endpoint coincides with an instant at the edge of the motion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00211

One definition of motion, given by Avicenna in The Salvation, is: “a body’s gradual change in a stable state, as it moves toward something and reaches it, whether that goal exists in potential or in actuality.” Let us explain each part of this definition and what it rules out. “A change in a stable state” excludes a transition from one unstable state to another, such as from one time to another, one action to another, or one experience to another. These are unstable states, and the transition between them is not motion, just as being in them is not rest. “In a body” excludes changes in the stable states of immaterial souls, such as universal acts of will and intellectual ideas. It also excludes, according to some, the changing readiness and receptivity of prime matter, though matter does have motion in its readiness and capacity. When we speak of motion in quantity, the matter itself is what moves; by “body,” we mean the body together with its matter.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00212

“Gradually” excludes change that does not occur bit by bit, such as the change of one substantial form into another, which Avicenna and most philosophers say cannot happen gradually. You will see the truth of this question in due course. “As it moves toward something” excludes, for example, a body’s gradual loss of light as it grows dark. Its stable state changes gradually, but this change is not a movement directed toward a goal. The word “toward” also marks an essential connection: the goal must be what the change directly and naturally reaches. This excludes gradual changes in stable states that do not essentially lead to the result that follows them. As we will explain in our study of final causes, a goal can be essential or incidental. This excludes a gradual change from one relation to another or one position to another when neither is an essential or primary goal; such a change follows from a change in something else. The definition includes both motions that have an actual endpoint, such as a straight-line motion that comes to rest, and motions that continue without reaching an actual endpoint, such as circular motion. The latter produces a gradual position that can be divided into positions that are still only potential.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00213

Another definition, given by a group of Muslim philosophers in agreement with earlier thinkers, is that motion is “leaving a state” or “passing from potentiality to actuality.” In The Healing, Avicenna calls this mistaken: “leaving” and “passing” are not a broader kind or anything like one; they are simply other words for motion. Motion and these words were first used for a body’s change of place, then extended to other changes. The closest definition, he says, is: motion is “reaching potential boundaries continuously,” while rest is when this reaching stops. This definition gives us motion as a continuous whole, which we will discuss.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00214

“Potential boundaries” is important here. A motion’s boundaries are only described as lying between its start and end; this points to what makes motion distinctive. The definition of motion as a continuous whole is then a description of it, rather than the kind of separate existence it has in the outside world.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00215
XI. What kind of existence does motion have?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00216

In The Healing, Avicenna says that motion has two meanings. The first is the continuous course the mind understands a moving thing to follow from its beginning to its end. This course does not exist as a completed thing in the outside world. As long as the moving thing has not reached its destination, the whole motion has not yet happened; when it has arrived, the motion has ended and is gone. So this kind of motion exists only in the mind. The moving thing recalls the place it left and the place it reached. When the image of its being in the first place is present in the imagination, and the image of its being in the second place is formed before the first image disappears, both images are present in the imagination. The mind then takes them together as one thing. Outside the mind, however, there is no independently existing whole motion between the endpoints. The moving thing is not present at either endpoint as it moves; it exists in the state between them.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00217

The second meaning is something that exists outside the mind: the body’s being midway between its starting point and its destination. At every boundary we imagine in that middle stretch, the body is neither before nor beyond it. This is a state that lasts as long as the thing is moving. The state itself does not change, though the body may change its position along the way as an incidental result. The body is moving not because it is at one particular intermediate point—for then it would stop moving as soon as it left that point—but because it is between the endpoints in the way described. This state is the same at every intermediate boundary. It is present in the moving thing at every instant, since at each instant it can be said to be at an intermediate point.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00218

When people say that every motion takes place in time, they may mean the first kind: the continuous course exists in time in the way past events do, though it differs from them because past events existed at some instant when they were present, while motion as a whole did not. Or they may mean the second kind: the body’s being between the endpoints is in time, not because it matches the whole span of time, but because it is accompanied by a process of covering distance, and that process matches the time. Since this state is present at every instant in that time, it lasts through the time by means of the process that accompanies it. That is Avicenna’s account.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00219

There are several points to examine and clarify. First, each nature has its own way of existing. A thing exists outside the mind when its definition applies to something and its defining limits are realized in it, as Avicenna says when he discusses relations. To say that something exists outside the mind means that its definition is true of things there. Motion, time, powers, and readiness are all like this. It is surprising that Avicenna holds that continuous time exists outside the mind, since it is divided into years, months, days, and hours. Motion as a continuous whole corresponds to this kind of time, and for him motion is the subject and cause of time. How can something that does not exist be the subject and cause of something that does?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00220

Second, perhaps Avicenna denies that motion as a continuous whole exists because the body is a stable substance, present at every instant of its existence, while motion itself is not present at any instant. If motion were a feature of the body in that sense, it too would have to be present at every instant that the body is present. He therefore says that the motion that exists is the other kind, since it lasts as long as the body does. But we say that the subject and recipient of motion is not the body considered as a fixed thing. It is the body through its matter, which is affected and changed from instant to instant. The mover, too—whether it acts by nature, force, or will—must undergo some change in its conditions so that, together with those conditions, it can bring motion about in what receives it. Avicenna himself explains this elsewhere: a changing effect must have a changing cause, and a stable effect a stable cause. The same applies to what receives the effect.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00221

Third, it is not right to deny all existence to motion as a continuous whole. Avicenna’s words here do say that, but we should understand him to mean that motion does not exist outside the mind as something complete, stable, and self-contained. His words point to this when he says it cannot exist as a stable, established thing, and that it has no stable existence outside the mind as it does there. In the mind, motion is formed gradually but remains all at once once the mind has formed it. Outside the mind, it comes to be and passes away gradually.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00222

Fourth, Avicenna’s explicit denial here seems to conflict with what he says elsewhere in The Healing. In his discussion of time, he says that arguments claiming time does not exist are based on the fact that it does not exist in an instant. But there is a difference between saying that something does not exist at all and saying that it does not exist as a completed thing in an instant. We can accept the latter: time has no completed existence in an instant, except in the mind or imagination. But time does have existence in a broader sense, outside the mind. If time did not exist, we could truly say that there is no interval in which something could cross a distance at a given speed. But that denial is false: there is such an interval. So time exists, even though it does not exist as a complete thing at any single instant. It does not exist merely because we imagine it: even if no one imagined it, it would still exist in this way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00223
Avicenna adds that some things have a firm, complete existence, while others have a weaker existence; time seems to have a weaker existence than motion. That is the end of his account.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00224

Avicenna is too great a thinker to contradict himself in one book. His point is that motion, which has a stronger existence than time, exists outside the mind in some way. Time depends on motion and is its measure, so motion must have external existence all the more. This is what Avicenna meant by denying that motion exists as a completed whole.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00225

Fifth, motion as “being between” does not exist outside the mind, someone might say, because it is universal. Universals, insofar as they are universal—open to many instances and shared by them—do not exist outside the mind. What exists in a particular motion is the body’s being at a particular point, and that is present in an instant. Some have therefore said that motion consists of successive positions along a distance, one after another. This would mean that instants follow one another and that adjacent boundaries touch. That is impossible. And if motion consisted of such separate positions, none would be a first completion of what is potential. Each would be a second completion, since motion is the process of reaching a particular position and seeking it, not the position itself. Seeking something is not the same as possessing it; moving toward a position is not being in it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00226

We answer that this kind of motion is indeed indeterminate in relation to the positions that the mind considers, whether at instants or over time. Still, it is made particular by the unity of its subject, the distance, the time, the specific mover, the starting point, and the destination. Motion is also one of the weak kinds of existence we have discussed. That much determination is enough, even if it includes a degree of sharing. The relation of the successive positions to motion as “being between” is like the relation of individual instances to a universal; their relation to motion as a continuous whole is like the relation of parts and boundaries to a whole.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00227

Sixth, someone might object that motion is either made up of parts that cannot be divided at all, or it is not. The first is false, as we showed in our discussion of bodies and quantities. The second means that motion can always be divided. Its imagined parts cannot all exist at once, since motion is not a stable thing. So they must exist one after another. If each part that exists is indivisible, then, once it ends, another indivisible part begins, and motion is made up of indivisible parts—which is impossible. If each part can be divided, then one part is earlier and another later; the whole part is never present. So what we assumed to be present is never present.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00228

I say that this objection, raised by al-Razi, is close to the earlier one. The mistake comes from forgetting that existence in general is broader than existence at an instant. We choose the second option: each part of motion that exists is potentially divisible into earlier and later parts, and this division can continue as far as the mind can carry it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00229

Seventh, one might say that the connection between the past and future parts of motion is a connection between something that exists and something that does not. We answer that motion and time are weak kinds of existence, in which existence is intertwined with nonexistence. Their actuality goes with potentiality, their coming to be with passing away. Each part calls for the nonexistence of another part; in a sense, it is itself its own passing away. Motion raises many questions, and there are many answers. We will not lengthen the discussion here; let us turn to what matters more.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00230
XII. Proving the First Mover
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00231

You now know the definition of motion: it is the first action or completion of something that is potential in some respect, precisely insofar as it is potential. The potentiality for motion is part of what makes a moving thing what it is as a moving thing. Rest stands opposite motion as absence stands opposite presence. We say that motion is an existing, possible feature, so it needs something able to receive it. Since it comes to be, it also needs an agent. The receiver and agent must be different: a thing cannot both bring about and receive the same changing action, since acting and being acted on are different categories; nor can the giver receive what it gives. A moving thing needs a mover; it does not move itself. A heater does not heat itself; it heats something that is only potentially hot.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00232

The recipient of motion must be potential, not actual. The agent that causes it must be actual in the respect toward which it moves the thing—that is, actual in the existence or completion brought about by the motion—even if it is not itself actual in motion, or potential for motion. Motion is not a completion of something already actual in the very respect in which it is actual. But there is a subtle point to notice.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00233

In existence there must be something other than motion and the thing that receives it: something that moves by its own nature and renews itself, and so is the source of motion by necessity. It has an agent or mover in the sense of something that brings its own renewing existence into being, not in the sense of a separate maker of its motion. There is no separate act of making between a thing and what belongs to its nature. The direct mover of motion must itself be moving; otherwise the cause would not accompany its effect. If motion did not ultimately depend on something whose own existence is renewed, we would face an infinite regress or a circle. We will return to this in detail, God willing.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00234

For now, we can say briefly that what receives motion is potential, either in the respect at issue or in every respect. What causes it is actual, either in that respect or in every respect. The different levels of actuality must end in something actual in every respect, so that we avoid circular reasoning or an infinite regress. In the same way, potentiality leads back to something potential in every respect, except that its potentiality itself is already actual. That is what distinguishes it from absolute nothingness.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00235

So existence has two extremes. At one end is the First Reality, pure existence—may His glory be exalted. At the other is prime matter. The first is pure good. The second has goodness only by accident. Since it is potential for all existing things, it is good by accident; unlike sheer nonexistence, which is pure evil. This also shows that a body is made up of matter and form. A body has the potential for motion, while its bodily form—the substantial continuity of its dimensions—is actual. So it contains a multiplicity of aspects. This points toward a profound idea: whatever is truly simple must contain all things in actuality. I have found no one on earth who knows this idea.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00236
XIII. Answering objections to the rule that every moving thing has a mover
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00237

The philosophers have handed down several arguments for this rule. First: if a thing moved itself, it could never rest, because what belongs to a thing by its own nature remains as long as the thing does. But moving things do rest. So the starting claim is false. Second: if a thing moved itself, all the parts of its motion would exist together as something fixed. Whatever is fixed is known to be fixed; if the motion were fixed, it would not be motion. Third: if a thing moved itself, it would either have a place or state that suited it, or it would not. If it did, it would not seek that place or state, and no direction of motion would be better than another. It would either move in every direction, which is impossible, or not move at all. If it had something that suited it, then once it reached that state it would rest. It would not, then, move itself.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00238

Fourth: if a body moved simply because it is a body, every body would move, since all bodies share bodyhood. That is false. If it moved because it was a particular kind of body, then that particular feature—not bodyhood—would be its mover. Fifth: as we saw in the previous chapter, potentiality and actuality are different respects. If a mover causes motion, it either moves without itself being moved, in which case it is not the moving thing, or it is itself moved. But to say that it is moved means that motion, which was only potential, has become actual in it. Motion would then be both potential and actual in the same thing, which is impossible. Sixth: as the recipient of motion, the moving thing is related to motion as something possible; as its agent, it is related to motion as something necessary. Possibility and necessity are opposites, so the mover cannot be the thing moved.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00239

In Eastern Investigations, al-Razi objects to the first three arguments. Is nature not a mover by itself, he asks, even though it does not move at all times? Do the imagined parts of motion not come and go? Does nature not seek a particular place? Why, then, could a body not move itself without any of the problems you describe? If you answer that nature calls for motion only when the body is in a state that does not suit it, or when it loses a state that does, and that new parts of motion arise as it grows nearer to or farther from the suitable state, then rest occurs once it reaches that state. But if a cause acts only while a condition is present, its effect does not continue once that condition is gone. So why could a body not call for motion only while it is in a state that does not suit it, with motion stopping once that state has passed?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00240

You cannot answer this, he says, without using the fourth argument: if bodyhood itself called for a particular state, all bodies would have it. The first three arguments therefore depend on the fourth. Let us examine that argument.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00241

Every body has a size, a bodily form, and matter. Its size consists of the three dimensions, which are plainly shared by all bodies. But we still need to prove that the bodily form is one and the same in every body. It cannot mean merely the ability to receive three dimensions. That ability is a relation, while bodyhood belongs to the category of substance. How could bodyhood itself be that relational capacity? Rather, bodily form is a substantial nature that entails the ability to receive dimensions.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00242

Once we establish that bodyhood is something that entails three dimensions, it is possible that this nature differs from one body to another even though all bodies share the ability to receive dimensions. Different things can share one feature that follows from them. Al-Razi then says: even if all bodies share one bodily form, they do not share the same matter. So suppose bodyhood is not the cause of motion. Why could a body’s particular matter not be the cause?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00243

I say that it is self-evident that all bodies share a substance that can receive dimensions. We do not need a proof of this to establish natural principles and particular movers. Motion, position, and location are all features of this shared substance. Only a three-dimensional body can be in a place. Position is the relation of a thing’s parts to one another and to something outside it. Moving from place to place is also an attribute of the body. The body must therefore be what receives these features and changes. Since the body is their recipient, they must also have an efficient cause beyond it. Philosophers give several arguments for this cause. Some begin from the potentiality of these features in the body: something that follows from a thing’s nature, or from its existence, may have one and the same subject as both recipient and agent. Others begin from the fact that different things have the same feature. If that feature followed from their shared nature, it would be found in them all in the same way. The philosophers also prove elsewhere that bodyhood is a shared kind of nature among the different kinds and classes of bodies.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00244

As for al-Razi’s claim that different things may share one feature that follows from them, we answer that this is possible only when the source of that feature is what they share, not what makes them different. We know that the ability to receive dimensions belongs to a body precisely as a body, not because bodies differ from one another. This meaning is shared by all bodies, even if their natures differ. Some of the arguments also show that different kinds of matter in bodies cannot be the source of the many distinct motions and effects special to each kind of body. Matter is only potential and ready to receive; its differences come from differences in natures and forms. That also answers the question why a particular matter cannot cause motion: matter is made particular only by a form that comes before it. We will see that actuality precedes potentiality in every kind of priority.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00245

Al-Razi adds that the heavenly sphere cannot come to be or pass away, so its shape, position, and size must necessarily belong to it. If this necessity comes from its bodyhood, even though not every body has those features, then motion too could belong necessarily to some bodies because of their bodyhood, without belonging to every body. If it comes from something present in bodyhood, then either that thing belongs to bodyhood or it does not. If it does not, what follows from it cannot belong necessarily to bodyhood. If it does, the same question comes up again. The only way out, he says, is to allow that the sphere’s shape and the other features do not necessarily follow from its bodyhood. Then perhaps the sphere could be broken apart or destroyed. Or perhaps those features necessarily follow from bodyhood in general, either directly or through something that belongs to bodyhood—even though they are not shared by every body. Motion could be the same way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00246

He then suggests that bodyhood is tied to its matter: because the heavenly spheres have matter unlike other matter, their matter could give them their shapes and dimensions. In that case, why could some bodies not have a particular kind of matter, unlike all others, that by its own nature produces a particular motion? This would not mean that all bodies share that motion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00247

I say that al-Razi’s argument about the heavenly sphere overlooks how an essence works, how a general kind is joined to the feature that makes it a particular kind, and how matter and form are connected in a compound thing. The heavenly form—and every particular form in a body—makes the body what it is. Bodyhood does not cause a thing to be heavenly, fiery, or watery, or to have the special features and effects that belong to each kind. We will explain this when we discuss forms. As for the claim that matter produces a particular motion and other special features, the “matter” described this way is really a form. It has the name of matter but not its meaning. The meaning given is exactly what we mean by form: the source of the effects special to a thing. Nature is the source of a thing’s own motion. Once proof has established what something is, we do not need to keep its old name.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00248

Al-Razi concludes that this argument cannot prove natural powers unless we first prove that matter is shared; otherwise, the argument fails. If matter cannot be the source of motion because it is only a recipient, and one thing cannot both receive and cause, we have already shown in our discussion of causes that this principle is false. Even if it were true, though, it would be enough to establish the conclusion. This is the fifth argument. The strongest objection to it, he says, is that essences cause their necessary features and receive them as well, which would disprove the rule that one thing cannot be both recipient and cause.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00249

I say that we have already explained the difference between acting and being acted on, and between potentiality and actuality—that is, possibility and necessity. The objection based on a thing’s necessary features does not apply. It rests on a misleading use of the word “recipient,” which can mean something that undergoes change, or something that is described as having a feature that necessarily belongs to it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00250
XIV. Dividing the moving power and proving an intellective mover
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00251

Some movers act in themselves; others act through something else, as a carpenter works through an axe. Some move a thing directly by giving it the quality of motion. Others do not act directly on its motion but give the moving thing itself a principle by which it can move, as we will explain. Some movers act by moving in turn; others act without themselves moving, like the beloved who moves the lover or the teacher who moves the student.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00252

Because there cannot be infinitely many bodies, there cannot be an infinite chain of moving things in which each moves another. We can see this, first, because a moving thing must be a body or depend on a body; an infinite chain of moving things would require infinitely many bodies. Second, causes must also come to an end. If the last moving thing is moved by a mover, and that mover is itself moved, then it cannot move until another mover has moved it. The middle term has two relations and a distinctive role: it moves and is moved. Whether there is one middle mover or many, and whether they are finite or supposedly infinite, motion cannot occur if every mover is only an intermediate link. There must be a mover that does not act like those in the middle of the chain.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00253

This brings what is potential into actuality. The source that brings something into being must itself be actual. It must exist in itself. So a mover that does not move must move either by giving a moving body the immediate principle by which it moves, or by acting as its goal, its good, or what it loves and knows. Every power in a body that moves also moves incidentally. A mover that does not move cannot therefore be a bodily power. We have shown that when a body produces a particular action or motion—not by accident, chance, or force—there must be an additional power beyond its bodyhood. That power is either a nature or a soul’s will. In either case, it must be connected to the body; it cannot be completely separate from it. If a particular action came from a source wholly separate from bodies and never connected with them, the separate source would be seeking through motion something it lacked. We have already shown this to be false. So if a separate mover contributes to the motion, it does so in one of the two ways just described, as in the motions of the heavenly spheres.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00254
XV. Why the immediate source of particular actions and motions is not separate from matter
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00255

Why can this particular body receive an effect from something separate from matter? There are only three possibilities: because it is a body, because it has a power within it, or because the separate being has a power that produces the effect. If the reason is simply that it is a body, then every body should receive the same effect, as we have already seen. But that is not what happens. If the reason is a power within this body, that is exactly what we are trying to show. If the reason is a power in the separate being, then either that power produces the effect by itself—in which case the same question about the separate being comes up again—or it acts by choice.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00256

If it acts by choice, then either it selects this body because of some feature in the body, or it affects the body at random. Random action cannot explain the lasting or usual order of the world, especially the order of the heavenly spheres. Chance does not produce results that always happen or happen most of the time. Natural actions, by contrast, do happen always or most of the time. As we will see, they are directed toward general purposes, not produced at random. So the effect must depend on a feature in the body itself. That feature is the body's nature: the power that moves it and through motion leads it toward its further completions, such as its proper place and shape. We will discuss this when we study bodily forms.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00257

This nature also restores a body when something unusual has disturbed it. When water is heated, when earth is forced upward, or when air is compressed, the nature within each returns it to its usual state once the outside cause is gone: water becomes cool again, earth returns downward, and air regains its natural lightness and spread. The same is true of a body that has become ill because one element has taken over. When its guiding nature grows strong enough, it brings the body back to a healthy balance.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00258
This also shows that the soul is not the body's temperament. A temperament that no longer exists cannot restore itself to its former state; what has ceased to exist cannot be brought back by itself.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00259
XVI. Every thing that comes to be is preceded by potentiality and the matter that carries it
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00260

Nothing can begin to exist unless there is first a potential for it to exist. Anything that comes into being after not existing must have matter that comes before it. Why? Before it exists, the thing is possible in itself. If it were impossible, it could never exist; if it were necessary, it could not have been absent. Its possibility is not the agent's power to bring it about. The thing is possible in relation to its own existence, not in relation to something outside it. This possibility must therefore be real before the possible thing exists. It is a feature of the world, not merely an idea in the mind or a way of speaking. It is a relation to the thing whose existence is possible. That relation is part of what makes the possibility what it is. Possibility taken in general is neither a substance nor a settled feature apart from this relation. If possibility were a substance, it would have its own existence, whether or not it was related to what might come to be. It would then be something existing on its own, rather than the ground of another thing's possibility.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00261

Nor can it be a settled feature that exists independently of the relation. We can see, then, that possibility in general does not first exist outside the mind and then acquire a relation to something else. What exists are particular possibilities, each related to the existence of a particular thing. This relation is part of the possibility itself, not an additional feature attached to it. Such possibilities are features of subjects. Because an accidental feature cannot constitute a substance, possibility itself must be an accidental feature existing in a subject. Let us call it the 'potential to exist', and call what carries it a subject, matter, or prime matter, depending on the way we consider it. This potentiality is real, even though it involves absence. Like existence in general, it is a shared meaning with many kinds beneath it, each a particular potential to exist in a particular way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00262

So every thing that comes to be is preceded by matter, and matter is one of the causes of coming to be. Whenever something comes to be or passes away, the matter of the thing that begins and the thing that ends must be one and the same. Otherwise, matter itself would have to come to be. It too would need prior potentiality and prior matter, and this would go on without end. This is impossible, though we will later explain one way matter can renew itself along with its form.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00263

The subject that carries potentiality must itself be a beginning with no earlier subject; otherwise, potentiality would need another potentiality before it, and the chain would never end. There is also another point: a potentiality that disappears when something becomes actual has a cause, and so must itself have come to be. It must have been preceded by another potentiality in time, and that earlier one by another, without end.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00264

Every matter, simply as matter, has the potential to become something actual. But the potentiality for a form means that the form can exist; it does not mean that the form itself needs to become actual, since form is already actuality. The possibility of a form is a feature of its matter. Think of the capacity of a basin: it is a feature of the basin. If you picture the basin and the amount of water it can hold, you understand the possibility of water being in it. Or think of the open space in a courtyard: once you picture the courtyard and the number of people it can hold, you understand the possibility of those people being there. This answers the question: how can something that exists be related to something that does not yet exist? The basin and the courtyard exist; their capacity is a real feature of them, directed toward what could fill them. Someone might say that a basin's capacity and a courtyard's space are positive features, while potentiality is negative. But these features are positive as features of their subjects and negative only in relation to what is not yet there. Potentiality taken in the broadest sense—the potential to exist at all—is absence in relation to existence.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00265

One point needs clarification. Some things are possible because they can exist in matter, such as bodily forms. Other things are possible only along with matter, not inside it; human souls are of this kind. Matter tips the balance in favor of a soul's existence rather than its nonexistence. Everything that could exist is equally possible to exist or not, so something must tip the balance. The giver of existence is generous and needs only a slight reason to bring a thing out of the middle ground between being and not being.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00266

This shows how matter causes a soul to come to be, and only in this way. Matter can be needed for two reasons: to help make up the thing that comes from it, or to tip the balance in favor of its existence. A rational soul is not made out of matter, so it needs matter only in the second way. Matter is a cause of things that come to be because it carries the potential for their existence and tips the balance toward their being rather than their not being. This will become clearer when we discuss the soul's life after death.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00267

Purely separate beings do not have real potentiality in the outside world. If they did, they would need something to carry it. Their possibility exists only as an idea in the mind: when we consider their general nature, we see that it is possible for them to exist, as explained earlier.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00268
XVII. Actuality comes before potentiality
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00269

The earlier chapters may have made it seem that potentiality always comes before actuality. Most people have held this view: matter before form, a general kind before its distinguishing feature, disorder before order, and the nature of a possible thing before its existence. But this is not so. In The Healing, Avicenna describes several views that place potentiality first. Some say matter existed before form, and that an agent later clothed it in form, either for no reason or because something prompted it. Some ancient thinkers even imagined that a soul accidentally took charge of matter, shaped it badly, and that God then stepped in and shaped it well.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00270

Others said that things had always been moving by their own nature in an irregular way, until God helped nature bring order out of disorder. Others said that darkness, a void, or a bottomless abyss had always existed in stillness and was later set in motion. Anaxagoras spoke of a mixture of all things. They based these views on examples such as seeds, semen, and things being made, where potentiality seems to come first.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00271

We answer that in particular examples of things that come to be and pass away, a particular potential may come before its result in time. But time order is not the important question. Potentiality as a whole comes after actuality in every kind of priority. It cannot exist by itself; it needs a substance to carry it, and that substance must already be actual. Something that does not exist at all cannot receive anything. There are also things that are actual and never potential, such as God and the separate intellects.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00272

Potentiality also needs an actual cause to bring it into actuality. That cause cannot itself be a new event that needs another cause, and that cause another, without end. The chain must reach something actual that did not come to be. We have already shown that causes cannot go on without an end. Actuality also comes before potentiality in understanding: we can understand a thing's power only by first understanding what it can do. And actuality comes before potentiality in value and completeness. Actuality is completion; potentiality is lack. Any capacity to act is directed toward the action that completes it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00273

Goodness belongs to what is actual. Harm and evil come from what is only potential, because it lacks some completion. Nothing is evil simply because it exists. It is evil because it lacks some good, as ignorance does, or because it brings about a lack in something else, as injustice does. Potentiality itself has a real existence, so its nature depends on existence, which is actual. We can therefore say that actuality comes before potentiality by cause, by nature, in value, in time, and in reality.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00274

There is a difficulty. Sometimes a capacity for evil seems better than the evil action itself. It is better to have the capacity to act unjustly than to act unjustly; being bad in actuality is worse than being capable of being bad. I agree, but only in comparison. Potentiality considered just as potentiality is a lack and so is bad. An evil action, such as injustice or illness, is an actual thing and so has existence, but it is bad because it causes a further lack. The capacity for that evil is better than the evil action because it is only a lack for an action that would cause another lack. The good in that capacity comes back to what is actual: avoiding the second lack. In the same way, the badness of an evil action comes from the potentiality and lack it brings about.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00275
XVIII. What is the subject of motion: the body or something else?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00276

We know that motion is a flowing state between pure potentiality and complete actuality. It includes a continuous passage from start to finish, which exists as a whole only in the imagination. Motion therefore needs something that is stable in some respect and can undergo it. That subject might be potential or actual. It cannot be only potential, because something with no actual existence cannot be described at all—not as potential, not as actual. So the subject must exist in actuality.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00277

It could be actual in every respect, or actual in one respect and potential in another. The first is impossible. Something actual in every respect is separate from matter and has no connection to it. Nothing like that can move from potentiality to actuality. It already has everything it could possibly have. Anything that can move still seeks something it does not yet have, so it cannot be fully actual. Anything fully actual cannot seek a goal through motion. Motion also comes to a thing as a feature, and the subject of any such feature must have some potentiality. A purely separate being has none.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00278
The subject of motion must therefore be a substance whose identity includes both actuality and potentiality. That is the body: its form makes it actual, while its matter remains potential.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00279

Motion cannot be the form that makes a kind of body what it is, for several reasons. First, motion is an accident, and one of the weakest kinds of being. It is the state of being moved, a relation; it is not the power by which a thing moves. So it cannot make a substance into the kind of thing it is. A thing cannot be made complete by something less complete than itself. Second, the subject of motion is a body that already exists. A completely general, undefined body exists only in the mind; outside the mind, every body already belongs to a particular kind. Third, kinds of motion do not exist as fixed, complete kinds in their own right. A thing that exists in a settled, actual form does not give another actual thing its kind. Fourth, if motion were part of what makes a body a particular kind, that kind would disappear whenever the body rested or any part of its motion ended. The kind would then be only potential and would need something stable and actual to carry it. So motion comes to a body only after the body already has its kind.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00280
This is the strongest account so far. Later, we will bring more light to the question.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00281
XIX. An Eastern insight
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00282

Motion is a thing's being moved, its renewal and passing away. Its immediate cause cannot be something whose existence is entirely fixed, or the parts of motion would never pass away. The agent that directly brings about motion must itself be renewed and moving. Motion must belong to it by its very existence. Anything whose existence necessarily includes motion still has a nature distinct from motion, but motion cannot be separated from that nature. Its motion is not something made separately from its existence. It follows from what it is.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00283

This makes motion an essential feature of the immediate mover's existence, not something added to it later. The immediate source of motion has a nature that remains the same, but an existence that is renewed. As we will see, the immediate source of motion in every kind of body is its nature: a substance that makes the body the kind of body it is. Nature is the body's first completion, in the sense that it is what makes a natural body an actual, existing body.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00284

So every body is renewed in its existence, even though its nature remains the same. This also shows that the material world comes to be in time: bodily substances and all their qualities, both those of the heavenly spheres and those of bodies made from the elements.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00285

What we said in the previous chapter—that the subject of motion must be stable—is true if “subject” means the thing's nature, which motion belongs to as a feature; or if we mean motions that are not essential to the thing's existence, such as moving from place to place, changing in quality, or growing. The same is true of the claim that the subject of motion includes both what is actual and what is potential, though this needs explanation. If motion belongs to the body as a feature, then the subject is made up of what is actual and remains through the motion, and what is potential and moving. Each part of motion appears and disappears while the body's nature remains. If, instead, the relation between motion and its subject is a matter of how the mind analyzes them, as with essential features, then the receiver and the agent are one thing, and actuality and potentiality are two sides of one reality.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00286

Here is the deeper point. Matter is potentiality and readiness; natural form comes to be anew, as we will explain. At every instant, matter is ready for a different form. Each new form has matter that is potential for it, and each form makes the matter actual. Since actuality comes before potentiality, this does not form a vicious circle. The forms are different in their nature, and matter changes its readiness with them. The matter of the elements is shared and remains through the changes; without something that remains, there would be no subject of motion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00287

Because simple bodies have forms that look alike, people have thought there is one form that stays with them. But their forms are not one and the same in number. They are one in kind and meaning, while continually following one another without a break. These are not separate, disconnected things. The result is one continuous, flowing existence. From its imagined boundaries, the mind draws out general natures such as human, animal, and plant.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00288
XX. Nature is the immediate source of motion in every moving thing
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00289

Nature is the immediate source of motion in every moving thing, whether the motion is natural, forced, or voluntary. In natural motion, this is clear: nature causes it. In forced motion, the force applied from outside only prepares the way; it is a cause in an indirect sense. That is why the forced motion can continue after the force has stopped. Besides, every outside force must ultimately lead back to nature or to the will.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00290

In voluntary motion, the soul moves the body by using nature. Many people who study these questions say that the soul is the immediate cause of motions that come from the will. But the closer cause, once imagination, will, and desire are present, is the power that moves the muscles, tendons, and ligaments. That power is the very nature of those body parts and tools. The soul sends it into them so that it can manage the body through them.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00291

We know by direct experience, even before we reason it out, that whatever inclines a body or turns it from one place or state to another must be an active power within it. This power is called nature. So the immediate source of bodily motion is a substantial power within the body. All accidental features depend on the form that makes a thing what it is, and that form is its nature. This is why philosophers define nature as the first source of a thing's own motion and rest, not of motion or rest that happens to it from outside. They have also shown that anything that can be pushed or drawn from outside must have a natural tendency of its own. So the direct source of every motion is nature.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00292

As we have seen, the thing that directly causes motion has a flowing, renewed existence. If it did not, it could not produce natural motions: something changing cannot come from something entirely unchanged. Philosophers such as Avicenna agree that nature cannot cause motion unless it changes. But they say that some outside change must affect it. In natural motion, for example, the moving thing keeps getting nearer to or farther from its goal. In forced motion, other states keep changing. In voluntary motion, particular wishes and desires arise in the soul as the reasons for acting change.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00293

I say that this does not solve the problem. All these changes must in the end lead back to nature. We have already seen that forced motion leads back to nature and that the soul can move the body only by using nature. So all these renewals depend on nature and are caused by it. Nature itself must therefore be renewed.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00294

Someone might reply that philosophers have shown how change, such as motion, can come from something fixed, such as nature. For each motion, they set out two linked sequences. One is the sequence of the motion itself. The other is a sequence of changing states in nature, such as the body's successive degrees of nearness to its goal. They say that each part of one sequence causes a part of the other, and is also caused by it in another respect. This, they argue, is not a vicious circle, as in the discussion of how something that begins can be connected to what is eternal.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00295

I say that this account does not explain how a changing thing comes from something fixed, or how something that begins is connected to what is eternal. The question is about the cause that actually produces motion, not the cause that merely prepares for it. Every effect needs a cause that brings it about. The two sequences may explain what sets the stages of a motion in order, but our question is what produces the motion itself. Motion is an effect, so it must have a cause that produces it and is always joined to it. If each sequence caused the other, each would have to come before itself.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00296

The only way out is to accept that nature is a flowing substance. Its changing reality arises between matter, whose character is to be potential and to pass away, and a pure agent, whose role is to give and pour forth existence. The agent continually brings forth something new in matter, and what was there passes away; then the agent replaces it without a break.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00297

Anyone who looks closely at both sequences together will see that they both come after nature already exists. This brings us back to the same question: if the starting point is fixed, how did these two sequences arise? It is like the argument against an endless chain of causes. If every link except the last is only a middle link, and there is no first link, where did the chain come from? Here too, if no being has renewal and passing away as part of its very nature, where did all the changing things come from, whether there is one sequence or many? And the successive degrees of nearness and distance that were treated as a second sequence are not separate from motion itself. Their renewal is motion, not something added to it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00298

So the changing things depend on something whose very reality flows and changes. That can only be nature. Separate intellects are beyond change and coming to be. The soul, considered in its intellectual nature, is also beyond change; in its connection with the body, however, it is nature itself, as we will explain later. Accidental features depend for their existence on substantial forms. Motion itself is not a thing that changes; it is the renewal and change of a thing. It is the relation of renewal, not something that causes renewal.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00299
XXI. How the changing is connected to the unchanging
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00300
Here, “actuality” means what exists now, and “potentiality” means what can exist or become real.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00301

Someone may ask: if every renewed thing is preceded by another renewed thing that causes it to be renewed, then the same question applies to the cause's renewal, and to the renewal of that cause's cause. This leads either to an endless chain, a circle, or change in the First Source—exalted far above that.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00302

Our answer is this. If renewal is not part of a thing's own nature, then it needs something to renew it. But if renewal is part of its nature, it does not need a separate maker to make it renewed. It needs a maker to bring the thing itself into being through a simple act, not through a second act that comes between the maker and what is made. There is no doubt that something exists whose very nature requires renewal and flow. We call it nature; others call it motion and time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00303

Everything has some stability and some actuality. What flows from the maker is the particular kind of stability and actuality that belongs to it. If a thing's stability consists in being renewed, and its actuality consists in having a capacity, then the First Source gives it that kind of stability and actuality. Every thing also has some kind of unity, which goes with existence and is one with it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00304

If a thing's unity is the unity of many things that are potential or actual, then the One gives it a unity that gathers multiplicity in one of these two ways. Of all existing things, nature is the one whose stability is renewal. Matter is the one whose actuality is potentiality. Number is the one whose unity is actual multiplicity. A body and what is in it have a unity that is the potential for multiplicity.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00305

So nature, in its stable aspect, is connected to the unchanging Source. In its renewed aspect, it is the link through which renewed things and new events come about. In the same way, matter, insofar as it has some actuality, comes from the active Source when form is joined to it. But insofar as it is potential and possible, matter is what allows bodily things to begin, pass away, and perish. These two substances—nature and matter—bring about change and passing away in bodily things through their own renewal and passing away. They connect what is eternal with what begins, and resolve a problem that has long puzzled careful thinkers.
